scope: static search for the phase-8 read-path gate

attempts.capstone_full_text: disassembling .text in one pass yields 0 references to 0x76446B0 because the linear sweep desynchronises on embedded data
attempts.byte_pattern: searching the little-endian immediate finds 240 candidate sites, but most are coincidental bytes (e.g. 0x4442F1 decodes as inc ebp); only sites on real instruction boundaries are useful

lesson: a linear capstone sweep over the whole section is not reliable for this binary; either walk from known function entries or validate each candidate against its surrounding instruction boundaries
next: start from known entries (CL_ParseServerMessage 0x473A50, the phase setter 0x5BE030) and disassemble per function instead of sweeping
focus on the frame loop that decides whether to read packets: find the caller of the read path and its clc.state comparison
then patch that gate so the client keeps reading at phase 8

0x473A50.note: disassembly around these addresses shows data, so the E8 matches are coincidental in embedded data

conclusion: caller discovery by raw E8 scanning also lands in data on this binary; use recursive disassembly from known entries instead
